chapter: Sansu, Irma, Lee Dorsey and the Meters
title: Putting the Meters together
summary: The Meters were already a group, Art Neville's band at the Ivanhoe; compared to Booker T and the MGs.

bands.name: Art Neville and the Neville Sounds

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: It does. It does. And not too long after that, I think it was in the late 60s, you all put together the meters. Were the meters together before they came to you all or did you kind of connect them up?
No, they were together very much so. Odd Neville and the Neville sounds. Planet of the Ivanhoe. Great little band.
I hope that makes some sort of sense.

It does, it does. And not too long after that, I think it was in the late 60s, you all put together the meters. Were the meters together before they came to you all, or did you kind of connect them up?
No, they were together, very much so. Art Neville and the Neville Sound, playing at the Ivanhoe. A great little band. And that's how they came.
And the song that came out at that time, no, I'll wait a little bit on that. So then they came into the studio. Did you see them at that point as being a New Orleans answer to Booker T and the MGs?
Had never thought about Booker T. But I guess whatever Booker T means in his area, or meant in his area, yes.
You know that emphasis on the organ instrumentals, piano instrumentals.

Well, I thought of them as instrumental groups, so the most, it consists of only rhythm sections, so it's not too much variation from that. You could get and still have the meters. Whether the solo be organ, piano, or guitar.
